rows.note: [Семифакторный навык в изучении] Семифакторный навык в изучении следует объяснять так: (1) как повторение вслух, (2) как повторение про себя, (3) в отношении цвета, (4) в отношении формы, (5) в отношении направления, (6) отношении места, (7) в отношении границ.

rows.pali: Imasmiṃ hi paṭikkūlamanasikārakammaṭṭhāne yopi tipiṭako hoti, tenāpi manasikārakāle paṭhamaṃ vācāya sajjhāyo kātabbo.
rows.english: 49. 1. This meditation subject consists in giving attention to repulsiveness. Even if one is master of the Tipiṭaka, the verbal recitation should still be done at the time of first giving it attention.
rows.note: Этот объект медитации состоит из направления внимания на отвратительность. Даже если человек является специалистом по Типитаке, повторение вслух всё равно должно выполняться в момент направления внимания на него в первый раз.

rows.pali: Ekaccassa hi sajjhāyaṃ karontasseva kammaṭṭhānaṃ pākaṭaṃ hoti malayavāsī mahādevattherassa santike uggahitakammaṭṭhānānaṃ dvinnaṃ therānaṃ viya.
rows.english: For the meditation subject only becomes evident to some through recitation, as it did to the two elders who learned the meditation subject from the Elder Mahā Deva of the Hill Country (Malaya).
rows.note: Дело в том, что для некоторых объект медитации становится очевидным через повторение вслух, как было в случае двух монахов, изучавших этот объект у учителя Маха Дэвы из страны гор (Малая).

rows.pali: Thero kira tehi kammaṭṭhānaṃ yācito cattāro māse imaṃyeva sajjhāyaṃ karothāti dvattiṃsākārapāḷiṃ adāsi.
rows.english: On being asked for the meditation subject, it seems, the elder [242] gave the text of the thirty-two aspects, saying, “Do only this recitation for four months.
rows.note: Когда они попросили объект медитации учитель дал им текст 32 частей тела со словами "В течение четырёх месяцев занимайтесь только повторением вслух.

rows.pali: Te kiñcāpi nesaṃ dve tayo nikāyā paguṇā, padakkhiṇaggāhitāya pana cattāro māse dvattiṃsākāraṃ sajjhāyantāva sotāpannā ahesuṃ.
rows.english: ” Although they were familiar respectively with two and three Piṭakas, it was only at the end of four months of recitation of the meditation subject that they became stream-enterers, with right apprehension [of the text].
rows.note: Хотя эти монахи были знакомы с двумя и тремя Никаями Канона соответственно, только в конце четвёртого месяца повторения вслух объекта медитации они достигли вхождения в поток с правильным пониманием текста.

rows.pali: Tasmā kammaṭṭhānaṃ kathentena ācariyena antevāsiko vattabbo "paṭhamaṃ tāva vācāya sajjhāyaṃ karohī"ti.
rows.english: So the teacher who expounds the meditation subject should tell the pupil to do the recitation verbally first.
rows.note: Поэтому учитель, объясняющий объект медитации, должен сказать ученику сначала повторять объекты вслух.

rows.pali: Karontena ca tacapañcakādīni paricchinditvā anulomapaṭilomavasena sajjhāyo kātabbo.
rows.english: 50.Now, when he does the recitation, he should divide it up into the “skin pentad,” etc., and do it forwards and backwards.
rows.note: Итак, когда он повторяет вслух, ему следует разделить список на "пятёрку кожи" и прочее и повторять их в прямом и обратном порядке.

rows.pali: Kesā lomā nakhā dantā tacoti hi vatvā puna paṭilomato taco dantā nakhā lomā kesāti vattabbaṃ.
rows.english: After saying “Head hairs, body hairs, nails, teeth, skin,” he should repeat it backwards, “Skin, teeth, nails, body hairs, head hairs. ”
rows.note: После слов "волосы головы, волосы тела, ногти, зубы, кожа", он должен повторить их назад: "кожа, зубы, ногти, волосы тела, волосы головы".

rows.pali: Tadanantaraṃ vakkapañcake maṃsaṃ nhāru aṭṭhi aṭṭhimiñjaṃ vakkanti vatvā puna paṭilomato vakkaṃ aṭṭhimiñjaṃ aṭṭhi nhāru maṃsaṃ, taco dantā nakhā lomā kesāti vattabbaṃ.
rows.english: 51.Next to that, with the “kidney pentad,” after saying “Flesh, sinews, bones, bone marrow, kidney,” he should repeat it backwards, “Kidney, bone marrow, bones, sinews, flesh; skin, teeth, nails, body hairs, head hairs. ”
rows.note: Затем с "пятёркой почек" после "плоть, сухожилия, кости, костный мозг, почки" нужно повторить это назад "почки, костный мозг, кости, сухожилия, плоть, кожа, зубы, ногти, волосы тела, волосы головы".

rows.pali: Tato papphāsapañcake hadayaṃ yakanaṃ kilomakaṃ pihakaṃ papphāsanti vatvā puna paṭilomato papphāsaṃ pihakaṃ kilomakaṃ yakanaṃ hadayaṃ, vakkaṃ aṭṭhimiñjaṃ aṭṭhi nhāru maṃsaṃ, taco dantā nakhā lomā kesāti vattabbaṃ.
rows.english: 52.Next, with the “lungs pentad,” after saying “Heart, liver, midriff, spleen, lungs,” he should repeat it backwards, “Lungs, spleen, midriff, liver, heart; kidney, bone marrow, bones, sinews, flesh; skin, teeth, nails, body hairs, head hairs. ”
rows.note: Затем с "пятёркой лёгких" после "сердце, печень, диафрагма, селезёнка, лёгкие" нужно повторить назад "лёгкие, селезёнка, диафрагма, печень, сердце, почки, костный мозг, кости, сухожилия, плоть, кожа, зубы, ногти, волосы тела, волосы головы".

rows.pali: Tato matthaluṅgapañcake antaṃ antaguṇaṃ udariyaṃ karīsaṃ matthaluṅganti vatvā puna paṭilomato matthaluṅgaṃ karīsaṃ udariyaṃ antaguṇaṃ antaṃ, papphāsaṃ pihakaṃ kilomakaṃ yakanaṃ hadayaṃ, vakkaṃ aṭṭhimiñjaṃ aṭṭhi nhāru maṃsaṃ, taco dantā nakhā lomā kesāti vattabbaṃ.
rows.english: 53.Next, with the “brain pentad,” after saying “Bowels, entrails, gorge, dung, brain,” he should repeat it backwards, “Brain, dung, gorge, entrails, bowels; lungs, spleen, midriff, liver, heart; kidney, bone marrow, bones, sinews, flesh; skin, teeth, nails, body hairs, head hairs. ”
rows.note: Затём с "пятёркой мозга" после "кишки, брыжейка, содержимое желудка, фекалии, мозг" нужно повторить назад "мозг, фекалии, содержимое желудка, брыжейка, кишечник, лёгкие, селезёнка, диафрагма, печень, сердце, почки, костный мозг, кости, сухожилия, плоть, кожа, зубы, ногти, волосы тела, волосы головы".

rows.pali: Tato medachakke pittaṃ semhaṃ pubbo lohitaṃ sedo medoti vatvā puna paṭilomato medo sedo lohitaṃ pubbo semhaṃ pittaṃ, matthaluṅgaṃ karīsaṃ udariyaṃ antaguṇaṃ antaṃ, papphāsaṃ pihakaṃ kilomakaṃ yakanaṃ hadayaṃ, vakkaṃ aṭṭhimiñjaṃ aṭṭhi nhāru maṃsaṃ, taco dantā nakhā lomā kesāti vattabbaṃ.
rows.english: 54.Next, with the “fat sextad,” after saying “Bile, phlegm, pus, blood, sweat, fat,” he should repeat it backwards, “Fat, sweat, blood, pus, phlegm, bile; brain, dung, gorge, entrails, bowels; lungs, spleen, midriff, liver, heart; kidney, bone marrow, bones, sinews, flesh; skin, teeth, nails, body hairs, head hairs. ”
rows.note: Затем с "шестёркой жира" после "желчь, слизь, гной, кровь, пот, жир" нужно повторить назад "жир, пот, кровь, гной, слизь, желчь, мозг, фекалии, содержимое желудка, брыжейка, кишечник, лёгкие, селезёнка, диафрагма, печень, сердце, почки, костный мозг, кости, сухожилия, плоть, кожа, зубы, ногти, волосы тела, волосы головы".

rows.pali: Tato muttachakke assu vasā kheḷo siṅghāṇikā lasikā muttanti vatvā puna paṭilomato muttaṃ lasikā siṅghāṇikā kheḷo vasā assu, medo sedo lohitaṃ pubbo semhaṃ pittaṃ, matthaluṅgaṃ karīsaṃ udariyaṃ antaguṇaṃ antaṃ, papphāsaṃ pihakaṃ kilomakaṃ yakanaṃ hadayaṃ, vakkaṃ aṭṭhimiñjaṃ aṭṭhi nhāru maṃsaṃ, taco dantā nakhā lomā kesāti vattabbaṃ.
rows.english: 55.Next, with the “urine sextad,” after saying “Tears, grease, spittle, snot, oil of the joints, urine,” he should repeat it backwards, “Urine, oil of the joints, snot, spittle, grease, tears; fat, sweat, blood, pus, phlegm, bile; brain, dung, gorge, entrails, bowels; lungs, spleen, midriff, liver, heart; kidney, bone marrow, bones, sinews, flesh; skin, teeth, nails, body hairs, head hairs. ” [243]
rows.note: Затем с "шестёркой мочи" после "слёзы, смазка, слюна, носовая слизь, синовиальная жидкость, моча" нужно повторить назад "моча, синовиальная жидкость, носовая слизь, слюна, смазка, слёзы, жир, пот, кровь, гной, слизь, желчь, мозг, фекалии, содержимое желудка, брыжейка, кишечник, лёгкие, селезёнка, диафрагма, печень, сердце, почки, костный мозг, кости, сухожилия, плоть, кожа, зубы, ногти, волосы тела, волосы головы".

rows.pali: Evaṃ kālasataṃ kālasahassaṃ kālasatasahassampi vācāya sajjhāyo kātabbo.
rows.english: 56. The recitation should be done verbally in this way a hundred times, a thousand times, even a hundred thousand times.
rows.note: Чтение нужно выполнять таким образом вслух сто раз, тысячу раз, даже сто тысяч раз.

rows.pali: Vacasā sajjhāyena hi kammaṭṭhānatanti paguṇā hoti, na ito cito ca cittaṃ vidhāvati.
rows.english: For it is through verbal recitation that the meditation subject becomes familiar, and the mind being thus prevented from running here and there,
rows.note: Ведь именно через чтение вслух объект медитации становится знакомым и тем самым предотвращается блуждание ума,

rows.pali: Koṭṭhāsā pākaṭā honti, hatthasaṅkhalikā viya vatipādapanti viya ca khāyanti.
rows.english: the parts become evident and seem like [the fingers of] a pair of clasped hands,15 like a row of fence posts.
rows.note: части тела становятся очевидными и будут заметны как пальцы сложенных вместе рук, как ряд заборных столбов.

rows.pali: Yathā pana vacasā, tatheva manasāpi sajjhāyo kātabbo.
rows.english: 57.2. The mental recitation should be done just as it is done verbally.
rows.note: Умственное чтение следует выполнять так же, как и чтение вслух.

rows.pali: Vacasā sajjhāyo hi manasā sajjhāyassa paccayo hoti.
rows.english: For the verbal recitation is a condition for the mental recitation,
rows.note: Ведь чтение вслух является условием для чтения про себя,

rows.pali: Manasā sajjhāyo lakkhaṇapaṭivedhassa paccayo hoti.
rows.english: and the mental recitation is a condition for the penetration of the characteristic [of foulness]. 16
rows.note: а чтение про себя является условием для постижения характеристики [непривлекательности].

rows.pali: Vaṇṇatoti kesādīnaṃ vaṇṇo vavatthapetabbo.
rows.english: 58.3. As to colour: the colour of the head hairs, etc., should be defined.
rows.note: "В отношении цвета": следует определить цвет волос головы и прочего.

rows.pali: Saṇṭhānatoti tesaññeva saṇṭhānaṃ vavatthapetabbaṃ.
rows.english: 4. As to shape: their shape should be defined too.
rows.note: "В отношении формы": их форма также должна быть определена.

rows.pali: Disatoti imasmiṃ hi sarīre nābhito uddhaṃ uparimadisā, adho heṭṭhimadisā, tasmā ayaṃ koṭṭhāso imissā nāma disāyāti disā vavatthapetabbā.
rows.english: 5. As to direction: in this body, upwards from the navel is the upward direction, and downwards from it is the downward direction. So the direction should be defined thus: “This part is in this direction. ”
rows.note: "В отношении направления": в этом теле, с пупка и выше - это верхнее направление, а ниже пупка - это нижнее направление. Поэтому направление следует определить так: "Эта часть в таком-то направлении".

rows.pali: Okāsatoti ayaṃ koṭṭhāso imasmiṃ nāma okāse patiṭṭhitoti evaṃ tassa tassa okāso vavatthapetabbo.
rows.english: 6. As to location: the location of this or that part should be defined thus: “This part is established in this location. ”
rows.note: "В отношении места": место той или другой части следует определить так: "эта часть находится в таком-то месте".

rows.pali: Paricchedatoti sabhāgaparicchedo visabhāgaparicchedoti dve paricchedā.
rows.english: 59. 7. As to delimitation: there are two kinds of delimitation, that is, delimitation of the similar and delimitation of the dissimilar.
rows.note: "В отношении границ": есть два вида разграничения - разграничений похожего и разграничение непохожего.

rows.pali: Tattha ayaṃ koṭṭhāso heṭṭhā ca upari ca tiriyañca iminā nāma paricchinnoti evaṃ sabhāgaparicchedo veditabbo.
rows.english: Herein, delimitation of the similar should be understood in this way: “This part is delimited above and below and around by this.
rows.note: Разграничение похожего нужно понимать следующим образом: "Эта часть ограничена сверху, снизу и вокруг вот этим".

rows.pali: Kesā na lomā, lomāpi na kesāti evaṃ amissakatāvasena visabhāgaparicchedo veditabbo.
rows.english: ” Delimitation of the dissimilar should be understood as non-intermixed-ness in this way: “Head hairs are not body hairs, and body hairs are not head hairs. ”
rows.note: Разграничение непохожего следует понимать как несмешанность следующим образом: "Волосы головы - это не волосы тела, а волосы тела не волосы головы".

rows.pali: Evaṃ sattadhā uggahakosallaṃ ācikkhantena pana idaṃ kammaṭṭhānaṃ asukasmiṃ sutte paṭikkūlavasena kathitaṃ, asukasmiṃ dhātuvasenāti ñatvā ācikkhitabbaṃ.
rows.english: 60.When the teacher tells the skill in learning in seven ways thus, he should do so knowing that in certain suttas this meditation subject is expounded from the point of view of repulsiveness and in certain suttas from the point of view of elements.
rows.note: Когда учитель объясняет навык в изучении этими семью способами, он должен обучать с учётом того, что в некоторых суттах этот объект медитации объясняется с точки зрения отвратительности, а в некоторых с точки зрения первоэлементов материи.

rows.pali: Idañhi mahāsatipaṭṭhāne (dī. ni. 2.377) paṭikkūlavaseneva kathitaṃ.
rows.english: For in the Mahā Satipaṭṭhāna Sutta (DN 22) it is expounded only as repulsiveness.
rows.note: В Махасатипаттхана сутте (ДН 22) он объясняется только как отвратительное.

rows.pali: Mahāhatthipadopama(ma. ni. 1.300 ādayo) mahārāhulovāda(ma. ni. 2.113 ādayo) dhātuvibhaṅgesu(ma. ni. 3.342 ādayo) dhātuvasena kathitaṃ.
rows.english: In the Mahā Hatthipadopama Sutta (MN 28), in the Mahā Rāhulovāda Sutta (MN 62), and the Dhātuvibhaṅga (MN 140, also Vibh 82), it is expounded as elements.
rows.note: В Махахаттхипадопама сутте (МН 28) и Махарахуловада сутте (МН 62) и в Дхатувибханга сутте (МН 140 и Вибханга 82) он объясняется в отношении первоэлементов.

rows.pali: Kāyagatāsatisutte (ma. ni. 3.153) pana yassa vaṇṇato upaṭṭhāti, taṃ sandhāya cattāri jhānāni vibhattāni.
rows.english: In the Kāyagatāsati Sutta (MN 119), however, four jhānas are expounded with reference to one to whom it has appeared as a colour [kasiṇa] (see III. 107).
rows.note: Однако в Каягатасати сутте (МН 119) четыре джханы объясняются в отношении того [из этой двойки спокойствие - прозрение?], в которой они проявляются как цвет (касина).

rows.pali: Tattha dhātuvasena kathitaṃ vipassanākammaṭṭhānaṃ hoti.
rows.english: Herein, it is an insight meditation subject that is expounded as elements
rows.note: В сутте это объект медитации прозрения, объясняющийся с помощью первоэлементов,

rows.pali: Paṭikkūlavasena kathitaṃ samathakammaṭṭhānaṃ.
rows.english: and a serenity meditation subject that is expounded as repulsiveness.
rows.note: и медитация спокойствия, объясняемая с помощью отвратительности.

rows.pali: Tadetaṃ idha samathakammaṭṭhānamevāti.
rows.english: Consequently it is only the serenity meditation subject [that is relevant] here.
rows.note: Следовательно, здесь речь будет идти только об объекте медитации спокойствия.

rows.pali: 181.Evaṃ sattadhā uggahakosallaṃ ācikkhitvā anupubbato, nātisīghato, nātisaṇikato, vikkhepapaṭibāhanato, paṇṇattisamatikkamanato, anupubbamuñcanato, appanāto, tayo ca suttantāti evaṃ dasadhā manasikārakosallaṃ ācikkhitabbaṃ.
rows.english: [The Tenfold Skill in Giving Attention] 61.Having thus told the sevenfold skill in learning, he should tell the tenfold skill in giving attention as follows: (1) as to following the order, (2) not too quickly, (3) not too slowly (4) as to warding off distraction, (5) as to surmounting the concept, (6) as to successive leaving, (7) as to absorption, (8)–(10) as to the three suttantas.
rows.note: [Десятифакторный способ направления внимания] Объяснив семифакторный навык изучения, он должен объяснить десятифакторный навык направления внимания следующим образом: (1) следуя порядку, (2) не слишком быстро, (3) не слишком медленно, (4) отгоняя отвлечения, (5) выходя за пределы концепции (6) постепенным оставлением, (7) поглощённостью, (8)-(10) тремя суттами.

rows.pali: Tattha anupubbatoti idañhi sajjhāyakaraṇato paṭṭhāya anupaṭipāṭiyā manasikātabbaṃ, na ekantarikāya.
rows.english: 62. 1. Herein, as to following the order: from the time of beginning the recitation [244] attention should be given following the serial order without skipping.
rows.note: "Следуя порядку": с момента начала чтения вслух следует уделять внимание соблюдению последовательности без пропусков.

rows.pali: Ekantarikāya hi manasikaronto yathā nāma akusalo puriso dvattiṃsapadaṃ nisseṇiṃ ekantarikāya ārohanto kilantakāyo patati, na ārohanaṃ sampādeti, evameva bhāvanāsampattivasena adhigantabbassa assādassa anadhigamā kilantacitto patati, na bhāvanaṃ sampādeti.
rows.english: For just as when someone who has no skill climbs a thirty-two-rung ladder using every other step, his body gets exhausted and he falls without completing the climb, so too, one who gives it attention skipping [parts] becomes exhausted in his mind and does not complete the development since he fails to get the satisfaction that ought to be got with successful development.
rows.note: Подобно неумехе, пытающемуся залезть на лестницу из 32 ступеней, и перепрыгивающему через каждую вторую ступень, тело которого устаёт и он падает не закончив своё восхождение, так и практикующий, направляющий внимание на этот объект и пропускающий части, умственно истощается и не завершает практику, потому что не получает удовлетворение, которое должно обретаться с успешной практикой.

rows.pali: Anupubbato manasikarontenāpi ca nātisīghato manasikātabbaṃ.
rows.english: 63. 2. Also when he gives attention to it following the serial order, he should do so not too quickly.
rows.note: А когда он направляет внимание следуя правильному порядку, ему не следует перебирать их слишком быстро.

rows.pali: Atisīghato manasikaroto hi yathā nāma tiyojanamaggaṃ paṭipajjitvā okkamanavissajjanaṃ asallakkhetvā sīghena javena satakkhattumpi gamanāgamanaṃ karoto purisassa kiñcāpi addhānaṃ parikkhayaṃ gacchati, atha kho pucchitvāva gantabbaṃ hoti, evameva kevalaṃ kammaṭṭhānaṃ pariyosānaṃ pāpuṇāti, avibhūtaṃ pana hoti, na visesaṃ āvahati, tasmā nātisīghato manasikātabbaṃ.
rows.english: For just as when a man sets out on a three-league journey, even if he has already done the journey out and back a hundred times rapidly without taking note of [turnings] to be taken and avoided, though he may finish his journey, he still has to ask how to get there, so too, when the meditator gives his attention to the meditation subject too quickly, though he may reach the end of the meditation subject, it still does not become clear or bring about any distinction. So he should not give his attention to it too quickly.
rows.note: Подобно человеку, отправившемуся в путешествие на 3 йоджаны, даже если он уже путешествовал туда и обратно 100 раз на большой скорости не обращая внимания на места, где следует повернуть, а где нет, хотя он может успешно закончить своё путешествие, ему всё равно придётся спрашивать как попасть туда. Поэтому когда практикующий направляет внимание на объект слишком быстро, хотя он и может достичь конца объекта, этот объект всё равно не станет понятен и не даст какое-либо достижение. Поэтому он не должен направлять внимание на него слишком быстро.

rows.pali: Yathā ca nātisīghato, evaṃ nātisaṇikatopi.
rows.english: 64. 3. And as “not too quickly,” so also not too slowly.
rows.note: И как следует избегать поспешности, также следует избегать и слишком медленного направления ума.

rows.pali: Atisaṇikato manasikaroto hi yathā nāma tadaheva tiyojanamaggaṃ gantukāmassa purisassa antarāmagge rukkhapabbatataḷākādīsu vilambamānassa maggo parikkhayaṃ na gacchati, dvīhatīhena pariyosāpetabbo hoti, evameva kammaṭṭhānaṃ pariyosānaṃ na gacchati, visesādhigamassa paccayo na hoti.
rows.english: For just as when a man wants to do a three-league journey in one day, if he loiters on the way among trees, rocks, pools, etc., he does not finish the journey in a day and needs two or three to complete it, so too, if the meditator gives his attention to the meditation subject too slowly, he does not get to the end and it does not become a condition for distinction.
rows.note: Подобно человеку, желающему завершить путешествие на 3 йоджаны за день, если он мешкает по пути среди деревьев, гор, озёр и прочего, он не закончит путешествие за день и ему потребуется 2 или 3 дня для прибытия в пункт назначения. Так и практикующий, если он направляет внимание на объект медитации слишком медленно, он не достигает конца и также это не становится условием для достижения.

rows.pali: Vikkhepapaṭibāhanatoti kammaṭṭhānaṃ vissajjetvā bahiddhā puthuttārammaṇe cetaso vikkhepo paṭibāhitabbo.
rows.english: 65.4. As to warding off distraction: he must ward off [temptation] to drop the meditation subject and to let his mind get distracted among the variety of external objects.
rows.note: "Отгоняя отвлечения": он должен отгонять искушение оставить объект медитации и позволить уму уходить в множество внешних объектов.

rows.pali: Appaṭibāhato hi yathā nāma ekapadikaṃ papātamaggaṃ paṭipannassa purisassa akkamanapadaṃ asallakkhetvā ito cito ca vilokayato padavāro virajjhati, tato sataporise papāte patitabbaṃ hoti, evameva bahiddhā vikkhepe sati kammaṭṭhānaṃ parihāyati paridhaṃsati.
rows.english: For if not, just as when a man has entered on a one-foot-wide cliff path, if he looks about here and there without watching his step, he may miss his footing and fall down the cliff, which is perhaps as high as a hundred men, so too, when there is outward distraction, the meditation subject gets neglected and deteriorates.
rows.note: Потому что если нет, то как человек, взошедший на горную тропинку шириной в одну ступню, если он будет смотреть в разные стороны не смотря куда ступает, он может оступиться и сорваться с горы, которая возможно высока как сто человек. Так и когда есть внешние отвлечения, объект медитации начинает игнорироваться и разрушается.

rows.pali: Tasmā vikkhepapaṭibāhanato manasikātabbaṃ.
rows.english: So he should give his attention to it warding off distraction.
rows.note: Поэтому он должен направлять внимание на объект, отгоняя отвлечения.

rows.pali: Paṇṇattisamatikkamanatoti yāyaṃ kesā lomātiādikā paṇṇatti, taṃ atikkamitvā paṭikkūlanti cittaṃ ṭhapetabbaṃ.
rows.english: 66. 5. As to surmounting the concept: this [name-] concept beginning with “head hairs, body hairs” must be surmounted and consciousness established on [the aspect] “repulsive.
rows.note: "Выходя за пределы концепции": нужно выйти за пределы концепции "волосы головы, волосы тела" и т.д. и установить ум на аспекте "отвратительный".

rows.pali: Yathā hi udakadullabhakāle manussā araññe udapānaṃ disvā tattha tālapaṇṇādikaṃ kiñcideva saññāṇaṃ bandhitvā tena saññāṇena āgantvā nhāyanti ceva pivanti ca.
rows.english: ” For just as when men find a water hole in a forest in a time of drought, they hang up some kind of signal there such as a palm leaf, and people come to bathe and drink guided by the signal, [245] body hairs,”
rows.note: Подобно тому как люди, нашедшие яму с водой в лесу в период засухи, вешают в том месте знак, например пальмовый лист, другие благодаря этому знаку приходят в то место пить и купаться.

rows.pali: Yadā pana nesaṃ abhiṇhasañcārena āgatāgatapadaṃ pākaṭaṃ hoti, tadā saññāṇena kiccaṃ na hoti, icchiticchitakkhaṇe gantvā nhāyanti ceva pivanti ca, evameva pubbabhāge kesā lomātipaṇṇattivasena manasikaroto paṭikkūlabhāvo pākaṭo hoti.
rows.english: but when the way has become plain with their continual traffic, there is no further need of the signal and they go to bathe and drink there whenever they want, so too, when repulsiveness becomes evident to him as he is giving his attention to the meditation subject through the means of the [name-] concept “head hairs,
rows.note: Но когда путь становится ясен благодаря непрерывному потоку людей, знак больше не нужен и они ходят купаться и пить туда в любое время когда захотят. Так и когда отвратительность становится для него очевидной и он направляет внимание на предмет медитации с помощью концепции "волосы головы, волосы тела",

rows.pali: Atha kesā lomātipaṇṇattiṃ samatikkamitvā paṭikkūlabhāveyeva cittaṃ ṭhapetabbaṃ.
rows.english: he must surmount the concept “head hairs, body hairs” and establish consciousness on only the actual repulsiveness.
rows.note: он должен выйти за пределы концепции "волосы головы, волосы тела" и настроить ум только на саму отвратительность.

rows.pali: Anupubbamuñcanatoti yo yo koṭṭhāso na upaṭṭhāti, taṃ taṃ muñcantena anupubbamuñcanato manasikātabbaṃ.
rows.english: 67. 6. As to successive leaving: in giving his attention he should eventually leave out any [parts] that do not appear to him.
rows.note: "Последовательным оставлением": в процессе направления внимания он должен со временем оставить те части, которые не проявляются ему.

rows.pali: Ādikammikassa hi kesāti manasikaroto manasikāro gantvā muttanti imaṃ pariyosānakoṭṭhāsameva āhacca tiṭṭhati.
rows.english: For when a beginner gives his attention to head hairs, his attention then carries on till it arrives at the last part, that is, urine and stops there;
rows.note: Потому что когда начинающий направляет внимание на волосы головы, его внимание затем продолжается до момента достижения последней части, т.е. мочи и на этом останавливается. .

rows.pali: Muttanti ca manasikaroto manasikāro gantvā kesāti imaṃ ādikoṭṭhāsameva āhacca tiṭṭhati.
rows.english: and when he gives his attention to urine, his attention then carries on till it arrives back at the first part, that is, head hairs, and stops there.
rows.note: А когда он обращает внимание на мочу, его внимание продолжается до момента достижения первой части, т.е. волос головы, и на этом останавливается

rows.pali: Athassa manasikaroto manasikaroto keci koṭṭhāsā upaṭṭhahanti, keci na upaṭṭhahanti.
rows.english: As he persists in giving his attention thus, some parts appear to him and others do not.
rows.note: По мере старания в таком направлении внимания некоторые части проявляются, а некоторые нет.

rows.pali: Tena ye ye upaṭṭhahanti, tesu tesu tāva kammaṃ kātabbaṃ.
rows.english: Then he should work on those that have appeared till one out of any two appears the clearer.
rows.note: Тогда он должен работать над теми, которые проявились, до момента когда одна из любых двух проявляется более ясно.

rows.pali: Yāva dvīsu upaṭṭhitesu tesampi eko suṭṭhutaraṃ upaṭṭhahati, evaṃ upaṭṭhitaṃ pana tameva punappunaṃ manasikarontena appanā uppādetabbā.
rows.english: He should arouse absorption by again and again giving attention to the one that has appeared thus.
rows.note: Он должен порождать поглощённость путём многократного направления внимания на ту наиболее ясную часть.

rows.pali: Tatrāyaṃ upamā – yathā hi dvattiṃsatālake tālavane vasantaṃ makkaṭaṃ gahetukāmo luddo ādimhi ṭhitatālassa paṇṇaṃ sarena vijjhitvā ukkuṭṭhiṃ kareyya, atha kho so makkaṭo paṭipāṭiyā tasmiṃ tasmiṃ tāle patitvā pariyantatālameva gaccheyya, tatthapi gantvā luddena tatheva kate puna teneva nayena āditālaṃ āgaccheyya, so evaṃ punappunaṃ paripātiyamāno ukkuṭṭhukkuṭṭhiṭṭhāneyeva uṭṭhahitvā anukkamena ekasmiṃ tāle nipatitvā tassa vemajjhe makuḷatālapaṇṇasūciṃ daḷhaṃ gahetvā vijjhiyamānopi na uṭṭhaheyya, evaṃsampadamidaṃ daṭṭhabbaṃ.
rows.english: 68.Here is a simile. Suppose a hunter wanted to catch a monkey that lived in a grove of thirty-two palms, and he shot an arrow through a leaf of the palm that stood at the beginning and gave a shout; then the monkey went leaping successively from palm to palm till it reached the last palm; and when the hunter went there too and did as before, it came back in like manner to the first palm; and being followed thus again and again, after leaping from each place where a shout was given, it eventually jumped on to one palm, and firmly seizing the palm shoot’s leaf spike in the middle, would not leap any more even when shot—so it is with this.
rows.note: Вот пример. Предположим охотник хочет поймать обезьяну, живущую в роще из 32 пальм, и он выстрелил из лука сквозь лист пальмы, стоявшей в начале, и крикнул. Тогда обезьяна прыгая с пальмы на пальму достигла последней пальмы, а когда охотник дошёл до неё и выстрелил и крикнул там, она аналогичным образом убежала к первой пальме. Будучи преследуема таким образом снова и снова, прыгая подальше от того места, где она услышала крик, она однажды прыгнет на одну пальму и крепко схватив посередине выступ с листьями, не будет больше прыгать, даже если в неё выстрелят, так и здесь.

rows.pali: Tatridaṃ opammasaṃsandanaṃ – yathā hi tālavane dvattiṃsatālā, evaṃ imasmiṃ kāye dvattiṃsakoṭṭhāsā.
rows.english: 69.The application of the simile is this. The thirty-two parts of the body are like the thirty-two palms in the grove.
rows.note: Применение этой метафоры следующее. 32 части тела подобны 32 пальмам в роще.

rows.pali: Makkaṭo viya cittaṃ.
rows.english: The monkey is like the mind.
rows.note: Обезьяна подобна уму.

rows.pali: Luddo viya yogāvacaro.
rows.english: The meditator is like the hunter.
rows.note: Практикующий подобен охотнику.

rows.pali: Makkaṭassa dvattiṃsatālake tālavane nivāso viya yogino cittassa dvattiṃsakoṭṭhāsake kāye ārammaṇavasena anusañcaraṇaṃ.
rows.english: The range of the meditator’s mind in the body with its thirty-two parts as object is like the monkey’s inhabiting the palm grove of thirty-two palms.
rows.note: Пространство ума практикующего в теле с его 32 частями в качестве объекта подобно обитанию обезьяны в роще из 32 пальм.

rows.pali: Luddena ādimhi ṭhitatālassa paṇṇaṃ sarena vijjhitvā ukkuṭṭhiyā katāya makkaṭassa tasmiṃ tasmiṃ tāle patitvā pariyantatālagamanaṃ viya yogino kesāti manasikāre āraddhe paṭipāṭiyā gantvā pariyosānakoṭṭhāseyeva cittassa saṇṭhānaṃ.
rows.english: The settling down of the meditator’s mind in the last part after going successively [from part to part] when he began by giving his attention to head hairs is like the monkey’s leaping from palm to palm and going to the last palm, [246] when the hunter shot an arrow through the leaf of the palm where it was and gave a shout.
rows.note: Утихомиривание ума практикующего в последней части после последовательного прохождения от части к части когда он начал направлять внимание на волосы головы подобно прыганию обезьяны с пальмы на пальму и достижения последней пальмы, когда охотник выстрелил из лука сквозь лист пальмы, на которой она сидела, и крикнул.

rows.pali: Puna paccāgamanepi eseva nayo.
rows.english: Likewise in the return to the beginning.
rows.note: То же самое с возвращением в начало.

rows.pali: Punappunaṃ paripātiyamānassa makkaṭassa ukkuṭṭhukkuṭṭhiṭṭhāne uṭṭhānaṃ viya punappunaṃ manasikaroto kesuci kesuci upaṭṭhitesu anupaṭṭhahante vissajjetvā upaṭṭhitesu parikammakaraṇaṃ.
rows.english: His doing the preliminary work on those parts that have appeared, leaving behind those that did not appear while, as he gave his attention to them again and again, some appeared to him and some did not, is like the monkey’s being followed and leaping up from each place where a shout is given.
rows.note: Его выполнение предварительной работы на появившихся частях, оставляя в стороне те, которые не проявились, когда он направлял внимание на них снова и снова и некоторые появились, а некоторые нет, - подобно преследованию обезьяны и её прыжкам прочь от тех мест, где раздаётся крик.

rows.pali: Anukkamena ekasmiṃ tāle nipatitvā tassa majjhe makuḷatālapaṇṇasūciṃ daḷhaṃ gahetvā vijjhiyamānassapi anuṭṭhānaṃ viya avasāne dvīsu upaṭṭhitesu yo suṭṭhutaraṃ upaṭṭhāti, tameva punappunaṃ manasikaritvā appanāya uppādanaṃ.
rows.english: The meditator’s repeated attention given to the part that in the end appears the more clearly of any two that have appeared to him and his finally reaching absorption, is like the monkey’s eventually stopping in one palm, firmly seizing the palm shoot’s leaf spike in the middle and not leaping up even when shot.
rows.note: Многократное направление внимания на одну наиболее ясную из любых двух частей, проявившихся ему и итоговое достижение практикующим поглощённости подобно тому, как обезьяна со временем остаётся на одной из пальм, крепко ухватив посередине выступ с листьями и не прыгая, даже когда в неё стреляют.

rows.pali: Aparāpi upamā – yathā nāma piṇḍapātiko bhikkhu dvattiṃsakulaṃ gāmaṃ upanissāya vasanto paṭhamageheyeva dve bhikkhā labhitvā parato ekaṃ vissajjeyya.
rows.english: 70. There is another simile too. Suppose an alms-food-eater bhikkhu went to live near a village of thirty-two families, and when he got two lots of alms at the first house he left out one [house] beyond it,
rows.note: Есть и ещё один пример. Представьте, что живущий на подаяние монах отправился жить в деревню, где живут 32 семьи, и когда он получил две ложки подаяния у первого дома, он обошёл следующий дом.

rows.pali: Punadivase tisso labhitvā parato dve vissajjeyya.
rows.english: and next day, when he got three lots of [alms at the first house] he left out two [houses] beyond it,
rows.note: На следующий день, когда он получил три ложки еды у первого дома, он обошёл два дома за ним.

rows.pali: Tatiyadivase ādimhiyeva pattapūraṃ labhitvā āsanasālaṃ gantvā paribhuñjeyya.
rows.english: and on the third day he got his bowl full at the first [house], and went to the sitting hall and ate—
rows.note: На третий день у первого дома ему наполнили едой весь сосуд для подаяния и он отправился в зал для сидения и там принял пищу.

rows.pali: Evaṃsampadamidaṃ daṭṭhabbaṃ.
rows.english: so it is with this.
rows.note: Так и тут.

rows.pali: Dvattiṃsakulagāmo viya hi dvattiṃsākāro.
rows.english: 71.The thirty-two aspects are like the village with the thirty-two families.
rows.note: 32 части тела подобны деревне с 32 семьями.

rows.pali: Piṇḍapātiko viya yogāvacaro.
rows.english: The meditator is like the alms-food eater.
rows.note: Практикующий подобен собирающему подаяние монаху.

rows.pali: Tassa taṃ gāmaṃ upanissāya vāso viya yogino dvattiṃsākāre parikammakaraṇaṃ.
rows.english: The meditator’s preliminary work is like the alms-food eater’s going to live near the village.
rows.note: Предварительная работа подобна тому, как этот монах пришёл на место проживания близ этой деревни.

rows.pali: Paṭhamagehe dve bhikkhā labhitvā parato ekissā vissajjanaṃ viya dutiyadivase tisso labhitvā parato dvinnaṃ vissajjanaṃ viya ca manasikaroto manasikaroto anupaṭṭhahante vissajjetvā upaṭṭhitesu yāva koṭṭhāsadvaye parikammakaraṇaṃ.
rows.english: The meditator’s continuing to give attention after leaving out those parts that do not appear and doing his preliminary work on the pair of parts that do appear is like the alms-food eater’s getting two lots of alms at the first house and leaving out one [house] beyond it, and like his next day getting three [lots of alms at the first house] and leaving out two [houses] beyond it.
rows.note: Продолжение направления внимания после оставления тех частей, которые не проявляются, и выполнение предварительной работы на тех частях, которые проявляются, подобно тому, как монах получил две ложки в первом доме и обошёл следующий за ним дом и как на следующий день он получил три ложки в первом доме, обойдя 2 следующих за ним дома.

rows.pali: Tatiyadivase ādimhiyeva pattapūraṃ labhitvā āsanasālāyaṃ nisīditvā paribhogo viya dvīsu yo suṭṭhutaraṃ upaṭṭhāti, tameva punappunaṃ manasikaritvā appanāya uppādanaṃ.
rows.english: The arousing of absorption by giving attention again and again to that which has appeared the more clearly of two is like the alms-food eater’s getting his bowl full at the first [house] on the third day and then going to the sitting hall and eating.
rows.note: Возникновение поглощённости благодаря многократному направлению внимания на то, что выглядит наболее ясным из двух, подобно тому, как этому монаху подали целый сосуд еды на третий день в первом доме и он пошёл в зал для сидения и принимает пищу.

rows.pali: Appanātoti appanākoṭṭhāsato kesādīsu ekekasmiṃ koṭṭhāse appanā hotīti veditabbāti ayamevettha adhippāyo.
rows.english: 72. 7. As to absorption: as to absorption part by part. The intention here is this: it should be understood that absorption is brought about in each one of the parts.
rows.note: "В отношении поглощённости": в отношении поглощённости часть за частью [тела]. Намерение здесь следующее: следует понимать, что поглощённость порождается в каждой части тела.

rows.pali: Tayo ca suttantāti adhicittaṃ, sītibhāvo, bojjhaṅgakosallanti ime tayo suttantā vīriyasamādhiyojanatthaṃ veditabbāti ayamettha adhippāyo.
rows.english: 73. 8–10. As to the three suttantas: the intention here is this: it should be understood that the three suttantas, namely, those on higher consciousness,17 on coolness, and on skill in the enlightenment factors, have as their purpose the linking of energy with concentration.
rows.note: "В отношении трёх сутт": намерение здесь следующее: следует понимать, что в трёх суттах, а именно в Нимитта сутте (сутте о возвышенном уме), в Ситибхава сутте (о прохладе) и в Агги сутте (о мастерстве в факторах постижения), целью является связывание усердия с собранностью уме.

rows.pali: Tattha –
rows.english: 74. 8. Herein,
rows.note: Здесь:

rows.pali: "Adhicittamanuyuttena, bhikkhave, bhikkhunā tīṇi nimittāni kālenakālaṃ manasikātabbāni.
rows.english: “Bhikkhus, there are three signs that should be given attention from time to time by a bhikkhu intent on higher consciousness.

rows.pali: Kālenakālaṃ samādhinimittaṃ manasikātabbaṃ.
rows.english: The sign of concentration should be given attention from time to time,

rows.pali: Kālenakālaṃ paggahanimittaṃ manasikātabbaṃ.
rows.english: the sign of exertion should be given attention from time to time,

rows.pali: Kālenakālaṃ upekkhānimittaṃ manasikātabbaṃ.
rows.english: the sign of equanimity should be given attention from time to time.

rows.pali: Sace, bhikkhave, adhicittamanuyutto bhikkhu ekantaṃ samādhinimittaññeva manasikareyya, ṭhānaṃ taṃ cittaṃ kosajjāya saṃvatteyya.
rows.english: If a bhikkhu intent on higher consciousness gives attention only to the sign of concentration, then his consciousness may conduce to idleness.

rows.pali: Sace, bhikkhave, adhicittamanuyutto bhikkhu ekantaṃ paggahanimittaññeva manasikareyya, ṭhānaṃ taṃ cittaṃ uddhaccāya saṃvatteyya.
rows.english: If a bhikkhu intent on higher consciousness gives attention only to the sign of exertion, then his consciousness may conduce to agitation.

rows.pali: Sace, bhikkhave, adhicittamanuyutto bhikkhu ekantaṃ upekkhānimittaññeva manasikareyya, ṭhānaṃ taṃ cittaṃ na sammā samādhiyeyya āsavānaṃ khayāya.
rows.english: If a bhikkhu intent on higher consciousness gives attention only to the sign of equanimity, then his consciousness may not become rightly concentrated for the destruction of cankers.

rows.pali: Yato ca kho, bhikkhave, adhicittamanuyutto bhikkhu kālenakālaṃ samādhinimittaṃ paggahanimittaṃ upekkhānimittaṃ manasikaroti, taṃ hoti cittaṃ muduñca kammaññañca pabhassarañca, na ca pabhaṅgu, sammā samādhiyati āsavānaṃ khayāya.
rows.english: But, bhikkhus, when a bhikkhu intent on higher consciousness gives attention from time to time to the sign of concentration … to the sign of exertion … to the sign of equanimity, then his consciousness becomes malleable, wieldy and bright, it is not brittle and becomes rightly concentrated for the destruction of cankers.

rows.pali: "Seyyathāpi, bhikkhave, suvaṇṇakāro vā suvaṇṇakārantevāsī vā ukkaṃ bandhati, ukkaṃ bandhitvā ukkāmukhaṃ ālimpeti, ukkāmukhaṃ ālimpetvā saṇḍāsena jātarūpaṃ gahetvā ukkāmukhe pakkhipitvā kālenakālaṃ abhidhamati, kālenakālaṃ udakena paripphoseti, kālenakālaṃ ajjhupekkhati.
rows.english: 75.“Bhikkhus, just as a skilled goldsmith or goldsmith’s apprentice prepares his furnace and heats it up and puts crude gold into it with tongs; and he blows on it from time to time, sprinkles water on it from time to time, and looks on at it from time to time;

rows.pali: Sace, bhikkhave, suvaṇṇakāro vā suvaṇṇakārantevāsī vā taṃ jātarūpaṃ ekantaṃ abhidhameyya, ṭhānaṃ taṃ jātarūpaṃ ḍaheyya.
rows.english: and if the goldsmith or goldsmith’s apprentice only blew on the crude gold, it would burn and

rows.pali: Sace, bhikkhave, suvaṇṇakāro vā suvaṇṇakārantevāsī vā taṃ jātarūpaṃ ekantaṃ udakena paripphoseyya, ṭhānaṃ taṃ jātarūpaṃ nibbāyeyya.
rows.english: if he only sprinkled water on it, it would cool down,

rows.pali: Sace, bhikkhave, suvaṇṇakāro vā suvaṇṇakārantevāsī vā taṃ jātarūpaṃ ekantaṃ ajjhupekkheyya, ṭhānaṃ taṃ jātarūpaṃ na sammā paripākaṃ gaccheyya.
rows.english: and if he only looked on at it, it would not get rightly refined;

rows.pali: Yato ca kho, bhikkhave, suvaṇṇakāro vā suvaṇṇakārantevāsī vā taṃ jātarūpaṃ kālenakālaṃ abhidhamati, kālenakālaṃ udakena paripphoseti, kālenakālaṃ ajjhupekkhati, taṃ hoti jātarūpaṃ muduñca kammaññañca pabhassarañca, na ca pabhaṅgu, sammā upeti kammāya.
rows.english: but, when the goldsmith or goldsmith’s apprentice blows on the crude gold from time to time, sprinkles water on it from time to time, and looks on at it from time to time, then it becomes malleable, wieldy and bright, it is not brittle, and it submits rightly to being wrought;

rows.pali: Yassā yassā ca piḷandhanavikatiyā ākaṅkhati yadi paṭikāya yadi kuṇḍalāya yadi gīveyyāya yadi suvaṇṇamālāya, tañcassa atthaṃ anubhoti.
rows.english: whatever kind of ornament he wants to work it into, whether a chain or a ring or a necklace or a gold fillet, it serves his purpose.

rows.pali: "Evameva kho, bhikkhave, adhicittamanuyuttena - pe - samādhiyati āsavānaṃ khayāya.
rows.english: 76.“So too, bhikkhus, there are three signs that should be given attention from time to time by a bhikkhu intent on higher consciousness … becomes rightly concentrated for the destruction of cankers.

rows.pali: Yassa yassa ca abhiññā sacchi karaṇīyassa dhammassa cittaṃ abhininnāmeti abhiññā sacchi kiriyāya, tatra tatreva sakkhibhabbataṃ pāpuṇāti sati sati āyatane"ti (a. ni. 3.103).
rows.english: [248] He attains the ability to be a witness, through realization by direct-knowledge, of any state realizable by direct-knowledge to which he inclines his mind, whenever there is occasion” (A I 256–58). 18

rows.pali: Idaṃ suttaṃ adhicittanti veditabbaṃ.
rows.english: - this sutta should be understood to deal with higher consciousness.
rows.note: - следует понимать, что в этой сутте рассматривается возвышенный ум.

rows.pali: "Chahi, bhikkhave, dhammehi samannāgato bhikkhu bhabbo anuttaraṃ sītibhāvaṃ sacchikātuṃ.
rows.english: 77. 9. “Bhikkhus, when a bhikkhu possesses six things, he is able to realize the supreme coolness.

rows.pali: Katamehi chahi?
rows.english: What six?

rows.pali: Idha, bhikkhave, bhikkhu yasmiṃ samaye cittaṃ niggahetabbaṃ, tasmiṃ samaye cittaṃ niggaṇhāti.
rows.english: Here, bhikkhus, when consciousness should be restrained, he restrains it;

rows.pali: Yasmiṃ samaye cittaṃ paggahetabbaṃ, tasmiṃ samaye cittaṃ paggaṇhāti.
rows.english: when consciousness should be exerted, he exerts it;

rows.pali: Yasmiṃ samaye cittaṃ sampahaṃsitabbaṃ, tasmiṃ samaye cittaṃ sampahaṃseti.
rows.english: when consciousness should be encouraged, he encourages it;

rows.pali: Yasmiṃ samaye cittaṃ ajjhupekkhitabbaṃ, tasmiṃ samaye cittaṃ ajjhupekkhati.
rows.english: when consciousness should be looked on at with equanimity, he looks on at it with equanimity.

rows.pali: Paṇītādhimuttiko ca hoti nibbānābhirato.
rows.english: He is resolute on the superior [state to be attained], he delights in Nibbāna.

rows.pali: Imehi kho, bhikkhave, chahi dhammehi samannāgato bhikkhu bhabbo anuttaraṃ sītibhāvaṃ sacchikātu"nti (a. ni. 6.85).
rows.english: Possessing these six things a bhikkhu is able to realize the supreme coolness” (A III 435).

rows.pali: Idaṃ suttaṃ anuttaraṃ sītibhāvoti veditabbaṃ.
rows.english: - this sutta deals with coolness.
rows.note: в этой сутте рассматривается высшая прохлада.

rows.pali: Bojjhaṅgakosallaṃ "pana evameva kho, bhikkhave, yasmiṃ samaye līnaṃ cittaṃ hoti, akālo tasmiṃ samaye passaddhisambojjhaṅgassa bhāvanāyā"ti (saṃ. ni. 5.234) appanākosallakathāyaṃ dassitameva.
rows.english: 78. 10. Skill in the enlightenment factors has already been dealt with in the explanation of skill in absorption (IV. 51, 57) in the passage beginning, “Bhikkhus, when the mind is slack, that is not the time for developing the tranquillity enlightenment factor …” (S V 113).
rows.note: Мастерство в факторах постижения уже рассматривалось в объяснении мастерства поглощённости во фрагменте Сукаракхата сутты, начинающимся с "Монахи, когда ум слаб - это не время для развития успокоения как фактора постижения"

rows.pali: Iti idaṃ sattavidhaṃ uggahakosallaṃ suggahitaṃ katvā idañca dasavidhaṃ manasikārakosallaṃ suṭṭhu vavatthapetvā tena yoginā ubhayakosallavasena kammaṭṭhānaṃ sādhukaṃ uggahetabbaṃ.
rows.english: 79.So the meditator should make sure that he has apprehended this sevenfold skill in learning well and has properly defined this tenfold skill in giving attention, thus learning the meditation subject properly with both kinds of skill.
rows.note: Поэтому практикующий должен убедиться, что он хорошо освоил семифакторный навык в изучении и должным образом разобрался с десятифакторным навыком направления внимания, тем самым должны образом овладев объектом медитации обоими видами навыков.

rows.pali: Sace panassa ācariyena saddhiṃ ekavihāreyeva phāsu hoti, evaṃ vitthārena akathāpetvā kammaṭṭhānaṃ suṭṭhu vavatthapetvā kammaṭṭhānaṃ anuyujjantena visesaṃ labhitvā uparūpari kathāpetabbaṃ.
rows.english: [Starting the Practice] 80.If it is convenient for him to live in the same monastery as the teacher, then he need not get it explained in detail thus [to begin with], but as he applies himself to the meditation subject after he has made quite sure about it he can have each successive stage explained as he reaches each distinction.
rows.note: [Начало практики] Если ему удобно жить в том же монастыре, где и учитель, то ему не нужно получать такое подробное объяснение в самом начале, но по мере того, как он прилагает усилия в практике предмета медитации после того, как он его полностью уяснил, ему можно объяснять каждую последующую стадию по мере достижения соответствующих успехов.

rows.pali: Aññattha vasitukāmena yathāvuttena vidhinā vitthārato kathāpetvā punappunaṃ parivattetvā sabbaṃ gaṇṭhiṭṭhānaṃ chinditvā pathavīkasiṇaniddese vuttanayeneva ananurūpaṃ senāsanaṃ pahāya anurūpe vihāre vasantena khuddakapalibodhupacchedaṃ katvā paṭikkūlamanasikāre parikammaṃ kātabbaṃ.
rows.english: One who wants to live elsewhere, however, must get it explained to him in detail in the way already given, and he must turn it over and over, getting all the difficulties solved. He should leave an abode of an unsuitable kind as described in the Description of the Earth Kasiṇa, and go to live in a suitable one. Then he should sever the minor impediments (IV. 20) and set about the preliminary work for giving attention to repulsiveness.
rows.note: Однако тому, кто хочет жить в другом месте, нужно дать объяснение по представленной схеме и он должен обдумывать его снова и снова, и все его затруднения должны быть разрешены. Он должен покинуть место неподходящего вида, как рассказывается в объяснении касины земли, и отправиться в подходящее место. Затем он должен устранить малые препятствия (см. гл. 4) и приступить к предварительной работе по направлению внимания на отвратительность.

rows.pali: Karontena pana kesesu tāva nimittaṃ gahetabbaṃ.
rows.english: [The Thirty-two Aspects in Detail] 81. When he sets about it, he should first apprehend the [learning] sign in head hairs.
rows.note: [32 части тела подробно] Когда он только приступает, практикующий должен сначала освоить [уловленное] представление в волосах головы.

rows.pali: Kathaṃ?
rows.english: How?
rows.note: Как?

rows.pali: Ekaṃ vā dve vā kese luñcitvā hatthatale ṭhapetvā vaṇṇo tāva vavatthapetabbo.
rows.english: The colour should be defined first by plucking out one or two head hairs and placing them on the palm of the hand.
rows.note: Сначала следует определить цвет путём вырывания из головы одного или двух волос и помещения их на ладонь руки.

rows.pali: Chinnaṭṭhānepi kese oloketuṃ vaṭṭati.
rows.english: [249] He can also look at them in the hair-cutting place,
rows.note: Он может также смотреть на них в месте стрижки волос,

rows.pali: Udakapatte vā yāgupatte vā oloketumpi vaṭṭatiyeva.
rows.english: or in a bowl of water or rice gruel.
rows.note: в сосуде для воды или в сосуде для рисовой каши.

rows.pali: Kāḷakakāle disvā kāḷakāti manasikātabbā.
rows.english: If the ones he sees are black when he sees them, they should be brought to mind as “black;”
rows.note: Если те, на которые он смотрит, выглядят чёрными, их следует отметить в уме как "чёрные",

rows.pali: Setakāle setāti.
rows.english: if white, as “white;”
rows.note: если белые, "белые",

rows.pali: Missakakāle pana ussadavasena manasikātabbā honti.
rows.english: if mixed, they should be brought to mind in accordance with those most prevalent.
rows.note: если несколько разных цветов, то нужно отметить в соответствии с тем цветом, который преобладает.

rows.pali: Yathā ca kesesu, evaṃ sakalepi tacapañcake disvāva nimittaṃ gahetabbaṃ.
rows.english: And as in the case of head hairs, so too the sign should be apprehended visually with the whole of the “skin pentad. ”
rows.note: И, как и в случае волос головы, представление следует сперва освоить визуально в отношении всей "пятёрки кожи".

rows.pali: 182.Evaṃ nimittaṃ gahetvā sabbakoṭṭhāse vaṇṇasaṇṭhānadisokāsaparicchedavasena vavatthapetvā vaṇṇasaṇṭhānagandhaāsayokāsavasena pañcadhā paṭikkūlato vavatthapetabbā.
rows.english: 82.Having apprehended the sign thus and (a) defined all the other parts of the body by colour, shape, direction, location, and delimitation (§58), he should then (b) define repulsiveness in five ways, that is, by colour, shape, odour, habitat, and location.
rows.note: Освоив таким образом представление и определив все остальные части тела по параметрам цвета, формы, направления, места и границ, ему следует затем определить отвратительность пятью способами, а именно цветом, формой, запахом, обитанием и местом.

rows.pali: Tatrāyaṃ sabbakoṭṭhāsesu anupubbakathā.
rows.english: 83.Here is the explanation of all the parts given in successive order.

rows.pali: Kesā tāva pakativaṇṇena kāḷakā addāriṭṭhakavaṇṇā.
rows.english: [Head Hairs] (a) Firstly head hairs are black in their normal colour, the colour of fresh ariṭṭhaka seeds.19

rows.pali: Saṇṭhānato dīghavaṭṭalikā tulādaṇḍasaṇṭhānā.
rows.english: As to shape, they are the shape of long round measuring rods.20

rows.pali: Disato uparimadisāya jātā.
rows.english: As to direction, they lie in the upper direction.

rows.pali: Okāsato ubhosu passesu kaṇṇacūḷikāhi, purato nalāṭantena, pacchato galavāṭakena paricchinnā.
rows.english: As to location, it is bounded on both sides by the roots of the ears, in front by the forehead, and behind by the nape of the neck.21

rows.pali: Sīsakaṭāhaveṭhanaṃ allacammaṃ kesānaṃ okāso.
rows.english: their location is the wet inner skin that envelops the skull.

rows.pali: Paricchedato kesā sīsaveṭhanacamme vīhaggamattaṃ pavisitvā patiṭṭhitena heṭṭhā attano mūlatalena, upari ākāsena, tiriyaṃ aññamaññena paricchinnā, dve kesā ekato natthīti ayaṃ sabhāgaparicchedo.
rows.english: As to delimitation, they are bounded below by the surface of their own roots, which are fixed by entering to the amount of the tip of a rice grain into the inner skin that envelops the head. They are bounded above by space, and all round by each other. There are no two hairs together. This is their delimitation by the similar.

rows.pali: Kesā na lomā, lomā na kesāti evaṃ avasesaekatiṃsakoṭṭhāsehi amissīkatā kesā nāma pāṭiyekko ekakoṭṭhāsoti ayaṃ visabhāgaparicchedo.
rows.english: Head hairs are not body hairs, and body hairs are not head hairs; being likewise not intermixed with the remaining thirty-one parts, the head hairs are a separate part. This is their delimitation by the dissimilar.

rows.pali: Idaṃ kesānaṃ vaṇṇādito vavatthāpanaṃ.
rows.english: Such is the definition of head hairs as to colour and so on.

rows.pali: 183.Idaṃ pana nesaṃ vaṇṇādivasena pañcadhā paṭikkūlato vavatthāpanaṃ.
rows.english: 84.(b) Their definition as to repulsiveness in the five ways, that is, by colour, etc., is as follows.

rows.pali: Kesā nāmete vaṇṇatopi paṭikkūlā.
rows.english: Head hairs are repulsive in colour

rows.pali: Saṇṭhānatopi gandhatopi āsayatopi okāsatopi paṭikkūlā.
rows.english: as well as in shape, odour, habitat, and location.

rows.pali: Manuññepi hi yāgupatte vā bhattapatte vā kesavaṇṇaṃ kiñci disvā kesamissakamidaṃ haratha nanti jigucchanti.
rows.english: 85.For on seeing the colour of a head hair in a bowl of inviting rice gruel or cooked rice, people are disgusted and say, “This has got hairs in it. Take it away.”

rows.pali: Evaṃ kesā vaṇṇato paṭikkūlā.
rows.english: So they are repulsive in colour.

rows.pali: Rattiṃ bhuñjantāpi kesasaṇṭhānaṃ akkavākaṃ vā makacivākaṃ vā chupitvāpi tatheva jigucchanti.
rows.english: Also when people are eating at night, they are likewise disgusted by the mere sensation of a hair-shaped akka-bark or makaci- bark fibre.

rows.pali: Evaṃ saṇṭhānato paṭikkūlā.
rows.english: So they are repulsive in shape.

rows.pali: Telamakkhanapupphadhūpādi saṅkhāravirahitānañca kesānaṃ gandho paramajeguccho hoti.
rows.english: 86. And the odour of head hairs, unless dressed with a smearing of oil, scented with flowers, etc., is most offensive.

rows.pali: Tato jegucchataro aggimhi pakkhittānaṃ.
rows.english: And it is still worse when they are put in the fire.

rows.pali: Kesā hi vaṇṇasaṇṭhānato appaṭikkūlāpi siyuṃ, gandhena pana paṭikkūlāyeva.
rows.english: Even if head hairs are not directly repulsive in colour and shape, still their odour is directly repulsive.

rows.pali: Yathā hi daharassa kumārassa vaccaṃ vaṇṇato haliddivaṇṇaṃ, saṇṭhānatopi haliddipiṇḍasaṇṭhānaṃ.
rows.english: Just as a baby’s excrement, as to its colour, is the colour of turmeric and, as to its shape, is the shape of a piece of turmeric root,

rows.pali: Saṅkāraṭṭhāne chaḍḍitañca uddhumātakakāḷasunakhasarīraṃ vaṇṇato tālapakkavaṇṇaṃ.
rows.english: and just as the bloated carcass of a black dog thrown on a rubbish heap, as to its colour, is the colour of a ripe palmyra fruit and,

rows.pali: Saṇṭhānato vaṭṭetvā vissaṭṭhamudiṅgasaṇṭhānaṃ.
rows.english: as to its shape, is the shape of a [mandolin-shaped] drum left face down,

rows.pali: Dāṭhāpissa sumanamakuḷasadisāti ubhayampi vaṇṇasaṇṭhānato siyā appaṭikkūlaṃ gandhena pana paṭikkūlameva.
rows.english: and its fangs are like jasmine buds, and so even if both these are not directly repulsive in colour and shape, still their odour is directly repulsive,

rows.pali: Evaṃ kesāpi siyuṃ vaṇṇasaṇṭhānato appaṭikkūlā gandhena pana paṭikkūlāyevāti.
rows.english: so too, even if head hairs are not directly repulsive in colour and shape, still their odour is directly repulsive.

rows.pali: Yathā pana asuciṭṭhāne gāmanissandena jātāni sūpeyyapaṇṇāni nāgarikamanussānaṃ jegucchāni honti aparibhogāni, evaṃ kesāpi pubbalohitamuttakarīsapittasemhādinissandena jātattā jegucchāti idaṃ nesaṃ āsayato pāṭikkulyaṃ.
rows.english: 87. But just as pot herbs that grow on village sewage in a filthy place are disgusting to civilized people and unusable, so also head hairs are disgusting since they grow on the sewage of pus, blood, urine, dung, bile, phlegm, and the like. This is the repulsive aspect of the habitat.

rows.pali: Ime ca kesā nāma gūtharāsimhi uṭṭhitakaṇṇikaṃ viya ekatiṃsakoṭṭhāsarāsimhi jātā.
rows.english: 88.And these head hairs grow on the heap of the [other] thirty-one parts as fungi do on a dung-hill.

rows.pali: Te susānasaṅkāraṭṭhānādīsu jātasākaṃ viya parikkhādīsu jātakamalakuvalayādipupphaṃ viya ca asuciṭṭhāne jātattā paramajegucchāti idaṃ nesaṃ okāsato pāṭikkulyaṃ.
rows.english: And owing to the filthy place they grow in they are quite as unappetizing as vegetables growing on a charnel-ground, on a midden, etc., as lotuses or water lilies growing in drains, and so on. This is the repulsive aspect of their location.

rows.pali: Yathā ca kesānaṃ, evaṃ sabbakoṭṭhāsānaṃ vaṇṇasaṇṭhānagandhāsayokāsavasena pañcadhā paṭikkūlatā veditabbā.
rows.english: 89.And as in the case of head hairs, so also the repulsiveness of all the parts should be defined (b) in the same five ways by colour, shape, odour, habitat, and location.

rows.pali: Vaṇṇasaṇṭhānadisokāsaparicchedavasena pana sabbepi visuṃ visuṃ vavatthapetabbā.
rows.english: All, however, must be defined individually (a) by colour, shape, direction, location, and delimitation, as follows.

rows.pali: 184.Tattha lomā tāva pakativaṇṇato na kesā viya asambhinnakāḷakā, kāḷapiṅgalā pana honti.
rows.english: [Body Hairs] 90.Herein, firstly, as to natural colour, body, hairs are not pure black like head hairs but blackish brown.

rows.pali: Saṇṭhānato onataggā tālamūlasaṇṭhānā.
rows.english: As to shape, they are the shape of palm roots with the tips bent down.

rows.pali: Disato dvīsu disāsu jātā.
rows.english: As to direction, they lie in the two directions.

rows.pali: Okāsato ṭhapetvā kesānaṃ patiṭṭhitokāsañca hatthapādatalāni ca yebhuyyena avasesasarīraveṭhanacamme jātā.
rows.english: As to location, except for the locations where the head hairs are established, and for the palms of the hands and soles of the feet, they grow in most of the rest of the inner skin that envelops the body.

rows.pali: Paricchedato sarīraveṭhanacamme likhāmattaṃ pavisitvā patiṭṭhitena heṭṭhā attano mūlatalena, upari ākāsena, tiriyaṃ aññamaññena paricchinnā, dve lomā ekato natthi, ayaṃ nesaṃ sabhāgaparicchedo.
rows.english: As to delimitation, they are bounded below by the surface of their own roots, which are fixed by entering to the extent of a likhā22 into the inner skin that envelops the body, above by space, and all round by each other. There are no two body hairs together. This is the delimitation by the similar.

rows.pali: Visabhāgaparicchedo pana kesasadisoyeva.
rows.english: But their delimitation by the dissimilar is like that for the head hairs.

rows.pali: 185.Nakhāti vīsatiyā nakhapattānaṃ nāmaṃ.
rows.english: [Nails] 91. “Nails” is the name for the twenty nail plates.

rows.pali: Te sabbepi vaṇṇato setā.
rows.english: They are all white as to colour.

rows.pali: Saṇṭhānato macchasakalikasaṇṭhānā.
rows.english: As to shape, they are the shape of fish scales.

rows.pali: Disato pādanakhā heṭṭhimadisāya, hatthanakhā uparimadisāyāti dvīsu disāsu jātā.
rows.english: As to direction: the toenails are in the lower direction; the fingernails are in the upper direction. So they grow in the two directions.

rows.pali: Okāsato aṅgulīnaṃ aggapiṭṭhesu patiṭṭhitā.
rows.english: As to location, they are fixed on the tips of the backs of the fingers and toes.

rows.pali: Paricchedato dvīsu disāsu aṅgulikoṭimaṃsehi, anto aṅgulipiṭṭhimaṃsena, bahi ceva agge ca ākāsena, tiriyaṃ aññamaññena paricchinnā, dve nakhā ekato natthi, ayaṃ nesaṃ sabhāgaparicchedo.
rows.english: As to delimitation, they are bounded in the two directions by the flesh of the ends of the fingers and toes, and inside by the flesh of the backs of the fingers and toes, and externally and at the end by space, and all round by each other. There are no two nails together …

rows.pali: Visabhāgaparicchedo pana kesasadisoyeva.
186.Dantāti paripuṇṇadantassa dvattiṃsa dantaṭṭhikāni.
rows.english: [Teeth] 92.There are thirty-two tooth bones in one whose teeth are complete.

rows.pali: Tepi vaṇṇato setā.
rows.english: They are white in colour.

rows.pali: Saṇṭhānato anekasaṇṭhānā.
rows.english: As to shape, they are of various shapes;

rows.pali: Tesaṃ hi heṭṭhimāya tāva dantapāḷiyā majjhe cattāro dantā mattikāpiṇḍe paṭipāṭiyā ṭhapitaalābubījasaṇṭhānā.
rows.english: for firstly in the lower row, the four middle teeth are the shape of pumpkin seeds set in a row in a lump of clay;

rows.pali: Tesaṃ ubhosu passesu ekeko ekamūlako ekakoṭiko mallikamakuḷasaṇṭhāno.
rows.english: that on each side of them has one root and one point and is the shape of a jasmine bud;

rows.pali: Tato ekeko dvimūlako dvikoṭiko yānakaupatthambhinisaṇṭhāno.
rows.english: each one after that has two roots and two points and is the shape of a wagon prop;

rows.pali: Tato dve dve timūlā tikoṭikā.
rows.english: then two each side with three roots and three points,

rows.pali: Tato dve dve catumūlā catukoṭikāti.
rows.english: then two each side four-rooted and four-pointed.

rows.pali: Uparimapāḷiyāpi eseva nayo.
rows.english: Likewise in the upper row.

rows.pali: Disato uparimadisāya jātā.
rows.english: As to direction, they lie in the upper direction.

rows.pali: Okāsato dvīsu hanukaṭṭhikesu patiṭṭhitā.
rows.english: As to location, they are fixed in the jawbones.

rows.pali: Paricchedato heṭṭhā hanukaṭṭhike patiṭṭhitena attano mūlatalena, upari ākāsena, tiriyaṃ aññamaññena paricchinnā, dve dantā ekato natthi, ayaṃ nesaṃ sabhāgaparicchedo.
rows.english: As to delimitation, they are bounded by the surface of their own roots which are fixed in the jawbones; they are bounded above by space, and all round by each other. There are no two teeth together …

rows.pali: Visabhāgaparicchedo pana kesasadisoyeva.
187.Tacoti sakalasarīraṃ veṭhetvā ṭhitacammaṃ.
rows.english: [Skin (Taca)] 93. The inner skin envelops the whole body.

rows.pali: Tassa upari kāḷasāmapītādivaṇṇā chavi nāma yā sakalasarīratopi saṅkaḍḍhiyamānā badaraṭṭhimattā hoti.
rows.english: Outside it is what is called the outer cuticle, which is black, brown or yellow in colour, and when that from the whole of the body is compressed together, it amounts to only as much as a jujube-fruit kernel.

rows.pali: Taco pana vaṇṇato setoyeva.
rows.english: But as to colour, the skin itself is white;

rows.pali: So cassa setabhāvo aggijālābhighātapaharaṇappahārādīhi viddhaṃsitāya chaviyā pākaṭo hoti.
rows.english: and its whiteness becomes evident when the outer cuticle is destroyed by contact with the flame of a fire or the impact of a blow and so on.

rows.pali: Saṇṭhānato sarīrasaṇṭhānova hoti.
rows.english: 94.As to shape, it is the shape of the body

rows.pali: Ayamettha saṅkhepo.
rows.english: in brief.

rows.pali: Vitthārato pana pādaṅgulittaco kosakārakakosasaṇṭhāno.
rows.english: But in detail, the skin of the toes is the shape of silkworms’ cocoons;

rows.pali: Piṭṭhipādattaco puṭabandhaupāhanasaṇṭhāno.
rows.english: the skin of the back of the foot is the shape of shoes with uppers;

rows.pali: Jaṅghattaco bhattapuṭakatālapaṇṇasaṇṭhāno.
rows.english: the skin of the calf is the shape of a palm leaf wrapping cooked rice;

rows.pali: Ūruttaco taṇḍulabharitadīghatthavikasaṇṭhāno.
rows.english: the skin of the thighs is the shape of a long sack full of paddy;

rows.pali: Ānisadattaco udakapūritapaṭaparissāvanasaṇṭhāno.
rows.english: the skin of the buttocks is the shape of a cloth strainer full of water;

rows.pali: Piṭṭhittaco phalakonaddhacammasaṇṭhāno.
rows.english: the skin of the back is the shape of hide streched over a plank;

rows.pali: Kucchittaco vīṇādoṇikonaddhacammasaṇṭhāno.
rows.english: the skin of the belly is the shape of the hide stretched over the body of a lute;

rows.pali: Urattaco yebhuyyena caturassasaṇṭhāno.
rows.english: the skin of the chest is more or less square;

rows.pali: Ubhayabāhuttaco tūṇironaddhacammasaṇṭhāno.
rows.english: the skin of both arms is the shape of the hide stretched over a quiver;

rows.pali: Piṭṭhihatthattaco khurakosasaṇṭhāno, phaṇakatthavikasaṇṭhāno vā.
rows.english: the skin of the backs of the hands is the shape of a razor box, or the shape of a comb case;

rows.pali: Hatthaṅgulittaco kuñcikākosakasaṇṭhāno.
rows.english: the skin of the fingers is the shape of a key box;

rows.pali: Gīvattaco galakañcukasaṇṭhāno.
rows.english: the skin of the neck is the shape of a collar for the throat;

rows.pali: Mukhattaco chiddāvachiddo kīṭakulāvakasaṇṭhāno.
rows.english: the skin of the face is the shape of an insects’ nest full of holes;

rows.pali: Sīsattaco pattatthavikasaṇṭhānoti.
rows.english: the skin of the head is the shape of a bowl bag.

rows.pali: Tacapariggaṇhakena ca yogāvacarena uttaroṭṭhato paṭṭhāya uparimukhaṃ ñāṇaṃ pesetvā paṭhamaṃ tāva mukhaṃ pariyonandhitvā ṭhitacammaṃ vavatthapetabbaṃ.
rows.english: 95.The meditator who is discerning the skin should first define the inner skin that covers the face, working his knowledge over the face beginning with the upper lip.

rows.pali: Tato nalāṭaṭṭhicammaṃ.
rows.english: Next, the inner skin of the frontal bone.

rows.pali: Tato thavikāya pakkhittapattassa ca thavikāya ca antarena hatthamiva sīsaṭṭhikassa ca sīsacammassa ca antarena ñāṇaṃ pesetvā aṭṭhikena saddhiṃ cammassa ekābaddhabhāvaṃ viyojentena sīsacammaṃ vavatthapetabbaṃ.
rows.english: Next, he should define the inner skin of the head, separating, as it were, the inner skin’s connection with the bone by inserting his knowledge in between the cranium bone and the inner skin of the head, as he might his hand in between the bag and the bowl put in the bag.

rows.pali: Tato khandhacammaṃ.
rows.english: Next, the inner skin of the shoulders.

rows.pali: Tato anulomena paṭilomena ca dakkhiṇahatthacammaṃ.
rows.english: Next, the inner skin of the right arm forwards and backwards;

rows.pali: Atha teneva nayena vāmahatthacammaṃ.
rows.english: and then in the same way the inner skin of the left arm.

rows.pali: Tato piṭṭhicammaṃ taṃ vavatthapetvā anulomena paṭilomena ca dakkhiṇapādacammaṃ.
rows.english: Next, after defining the inner skin of the back, he should define the inner skin of the right leg forwards and backwards;

rows.pali: Atha teneva nayena vāmapādacammaṃ.
rows.english: then the inner skin of the left leg in the same way.

rows.pali: Tato anukkameneva vatthiudarahadayagīvacammāni vavatthapetabbāni.
rows.english: Next, the inner skin of the groin, the paunch, the bosom and the neck should be successively defined.

rows.pali: Atha gīvacammānantaraṃ heṭṭhimahanucammaṃ vavatthapetvā adharoṭṭhapariyosānaṃ pāpetvā niṭṭhapetabbaṃ.
rows.english: Then, after defining the inner skin of the lower jaw next after that of the neck, he should finish on arriving at the lower lip.

rows.pali: Evaṃ oḷārikoḷārikaṃ pariggaṇhantassa sukhumampi pākaṭaṃ hoti.
rows.english: When he discerns it in the gross in this way, it becomes evident to him more subtly too.

rows.pali: Disato dvīsu disāsu jāto.
rows.english: 96.As to direction, it lies in both directions.

rows.pali: Okāsato sakalasarīraṃ pariyonandhitvā ṭhito.
rows.english: As to location, it covers the whole body.

rows.pali: Paricchedato heṭṭhā patiṭṭhitatalena, upari ākāsena paricchinno, ayamassa sabhāgaparicchedo.
rows.english: As to delimitation, it is bounded below by its fixed surface, and above by space …

rows.pali: Visabhāgaparicchedo pana kesasadisoyeva.
188.Maṃsanti nava maṃsapesisatāni.
rows.english: [Flesh] 97.There are nine hundred pieces of flesh.

rows.pali: Taṃ sabbampi vaṇṇato rattaṃ kiṃsukapupphasadisaṃ.
rows.english: As to colour, it is all red, like kiṃsuka flowers.

rows.pali: Saṇṭhānato jaṅghapiṇḍikamaṃsaṃ tālapaṇṇapuṭabhattasaṇṭhānaṃ.
rows.english: As to shape, the flesh of the calves is the shape of cooked rice in a palm- leaf bag.

rows.pali: Ūrumaṃsaṃ nisadapotasaṇṭhānaṃ.
rows.english: The flesh of the thighs is the shape of a rolling pin.23

rows.pali: Ānisadamaṃsaṃ uddhanakoṭisaṇṭhānaṃ.
rows.english: The flesh of the buttocks is the shape of the end of an oven.

rows.pali: Piṭṭhimaṃsaṃ tālaguḷapaṭalasaṇṭhānaṃ.
rows.english: The flesh of the back is the shape of a slab of palm sugar.

rows.pali: Phāsukadvayamaṃsaṃ koṭṭhalikāya kucchiyaṃ tanumattikālepasaṇṭhānaṃ.
rows.english: The flesh between each two ribs is the shape of clay mortar squeezed thin in a flattened opening.

rows.pali: Thanamaṃsaṃ vaṭṭetvā avakkhittamattikāpiṇḍasaṇṭhānaṃ.
rows.english: The flesh of the breast is the shape of a lump of clay made into a ball and flung down.

rows.pali: Bāhudvayamaṃsaṃ dviguṇaṃ katvā ṭhapitaniccammamahāmūsikasaṇṭhānaṃ.
rows.english: The flesh of the two upper arms is the shape of a large skinned rat and twice the size.

rows.pali: Evaṃ oḷārikoḷārikaṃ pariggaṇhantassa sukhumampi pākaṭaṃ hoti.
rows.english: When he discerns it grossly in this way, it becomes evident to him subtly too.

rows.pali: Disato dvīsu disāsu jātaṃ.
rows.english: 98.As to direction, it lies in both directions.

rows.pali: Okāsato vīsādhikāni tīṇi aṭṭhisatāni anulimpitvā ṭhitaṃ.
rows.english: As to location, it is plastered over the three hundred and odd bones.

rows.pali: Paricchedato heṭṭhā aṭṭhisaṅghāte patiṭṭhitatalena, upari tacena, tiriyaṃ aññamaññena paricchinnaṃ, ayamassa sabhāgaparicchedo.
rows.english: As to delimitation, it is bounded below by its surface, which is fixed on to the collection of bones, and above by the skin, and all round each by each other piece …

rows.pali: Visabhāgaparicchedo pana kesasadisoyeva.
189.Nhārūti nava nhārusatāni.
rows.english: [Sinews] 99.There are nine hundred sinews.

rows.pali: Vaṇṇato sabbepi nhārū setā.
rows.english: As to colour, all the sinews are white.

rows.pali: Saṇṭhānato nānāsaṇṭhānā.
rows.english: As to shape, they have various shapes.

rows.pali: Etesu hi gīvāya uparimabhāgato paṭṭhāya pañca mahānhārū sarīraṃ vinandhamānā purimapassena otiṇṇā.
rows.english: For five of great sinews that bind the body together start out from the upper part of the neck and descend by the front,

rows.pali: Pañca pacchimapassena.
rows.english: and five more by the back,

rows.pali: Pañca dakkhiṇapassena.
rows.english: and then five by the right

rows.pali: Pañca vāmapassena.
rows.english: and five by the left.

rows.pali: Dakkhiṇahatthaṃ vinandhamānāpi hatthassa purimapassena pañca.
rows.english: And of those that bind the right hand, five descend by the front of the hand

rows.pali: Pacchimapassena pañca.
rows.english: and five by the back;

rows.pali: Tathā vāmahatthaṃ vinandhamānā.
rows.english: likewise those that bind the left hand.

rows.pali: Dakkhiṇapādaṃ vinandhamānāpi pādassa purimapassena pañca.
rows.english: And of those that bind the right foot, five descend by the front and five by the back;

rows.pali: Pacchimapassena pañca.
rows.english: likewise those that bind the left foot.

rows.pali: Tathā vāmapādaṃ vinandhamānāpīti evaṃ sarīradhārakā nāma saṭṭhimahānhārū kāyaṃ vinandhamānā otiṇṇā.
rows.english: So there are sixty great sinews called “body supporters” which descend [from the neck] and bind the body together;

rows.pali: Ye kaṇḍarātipi vuccanti.
rows.english: and they are also called “tendons.”

rows.pali: Te sabbepi kandalamakuḷasaṇṭhānā.
rows.english: They are all the shape of yam shoots.

rows.pali: Aññe pana taṃ taṃ padesaṃ ajjhottharitvā ṭhitā.
rows.english: But there are others scattered over various parts of the body,

rows.pali: Tato sukhumatarā suttarajjukasaṇṭhānā.
rows.english: which are finer than the last-named. They are the shape of strings and cords.

rows.pali: Aññe tato sukhumatarā pūtilatāsaṇṭhānā, aññe tato sukhumatarā mahāvīṇātantisaṇṭhānā.
rows.english: There are others still finer, the shape of creepers. Others still finer are the shape of large lute strings.

rows.pali: Aññe thūlasuttakasaṇṭhānā.
rows.english: Yet others are the shape of coarse thread.

rows.pali: Hatthapādapiṭṭhīsu nhārū sakuṇapādasaṇṭhānā.
rows.english: The sinews in the backs of the hands and feet are the shape of a bird’s claw.

rows.pali: Sīse nhārū dārakānaṃ sīsajālakasaṇṭhānā.
rows.english: The sinews in the head are the shape of children’s head nets.

rows.pali: Piṭṭhiyaṃ nhārū ātape pasāritaallajālasaṇṭhānā.
rows.english: The sinews in the back are the shape of a wet net spread out in the sun.

rows.pali: Avasesā taṃtaṃaṅgapaccaṅgānugatā nhārū sarīre paṭimukkajālakañcukasaṇṭhānā.
rows.english: The rest of the sinews, following the various limbs, are the shape of a net jacket fitted to the body.

rows.pali: Disato dvīsu disāsu jātā.
rows.english: 100.As to direction, they lie in the two directions.

rows.pali: Okāsato sakalasarīre aṭṭhīni ābandhitvā ṭhitā.
rows.english: As to location, they are to be found binding the bones of the whole body together.

rows.pali: Paricchedato heṭṭhā tiṇṇaṃ aṭṭhisatānaṃ upari patiṭṭhitatalehi, upari maṃsacammāni āhacca ṭhitappadesehi, tiriyaṃ aññamaññena paricchinnā, ayaṃ nesaṃ sabhāgaparicchedo.
rows.english: As to delimitation, they are bounded below by their surface, which is fixed on to the three hundred bones, and above by the portions that are in contact with the flesh and the inner skin, and all round by each other …

rows.pali: Visabhāgaparicchedo pana kesasadisoyeva.

190.Aṭṭhīti ṭhapetvā dvattiṃsa dantaṭṭhīni avasesāni catusaṭṭhi hatthaṭṭhīni, catusaṭṭhi pādaṭṭhīni, catusaṭṭhi maṃsanissitāni muduaṭṭhīni, dve paṇhikaṭṭhīni, ekekasmiṃ pāde dve dve gopphakaṭṭhīni, dve jaṅghaṭṭhīni, ekaṃ jaṇṇukaṭṭhi, ekaṃ ūruṭṭhi, dve kaṭiṭṭhīni, aṭṭhārasa piṭṭhikaṇṭakaṭṭhīni, catuvīsati phāsukaṭṭhīni, cuddasa uraṭṭhīni, ekaṃ hadayaṭṭhi, dve akkhakaṭṭhīni, dve koṭṭaṭṭhīni, dve bāhuṭṭhīni, dve dve aggabāhuṭṭhīni, satta gīvaṭṭhīni, dve hanukaṭṭhīni, ekaṃ nāsikaṭṭhi, dve akkhiṭṭhīni, dve kaṇṇaṭṭhīni, ekaṃ nalāṭaṭṭhi.
rows.english: [Bones] 101. Excepting the thirty-two teeth bones, these consist of the remaining sixty- four hand bones, sixty-four foot bones, sixty-four soft bones dependent on the flesh, two heel bones; then in each leg two ankle bones, two shin bones, one knee bone and one thigh bone; then two hip bones, eighteen spine bones, twenty- four rib bones, fourteen breast bones, one heart bone (sternum), two collar bones, two shoulder blade bones,24 two upper-arm bones, two pairs of forearm bones, two neck bones, two jaw bones, one nose bone, two eye bones, two ear bones, one frontal bone,

rows.pali: Ekaṃ muddhaṭṭhi, nava sīsakapālaṭṭhīnīti evaṃ timattāni aṭṭhisatāni, tāni sabbānipi vaṇṇato setāni.
rows.english: one occipital bone, nine sincipital bones. So there are exactly three hundred bones. As to colour, they are all white.

rows.pali: Saṇṭhānato nānāsaṇṭhānāni.
rows.english: As to shape, they are of various shapes.

rows.pali: Tattha hi aggapādaṅguliaṭṭhīni katakabījasaṇṭhānāni.
rows.english: 102.Herein, the end bones of the toes are the shape of kataka seeds.

rows.pali: Tadanantarāni majjhapabbaṭṭhīni panasaṭṭhisaṇṭhānāni.
rows.english: Those next to them in the middle sections are the shape of jackfruit seeds.

rows.pali: Mūlapabbaṭṭhīni paṇavasaṇṭhānāni.
rows.english: The bones of the base sections are the shape of small drums.

rows.pali: Piṭṭhipādaṭṭhīni koṭṭitakandalakandarāsisaṇṭhānāni.
rows.english: The bones of the back of the foot are the shape of a bunch of bruised yarns.

rows.pali: Paṇhikaṭṭhi ekaṭṭhitālaphalabījasaṇṭhānaṃ.
rows.english: The heel bone is the shape of the seed of a single-stone palmyra fruit.

rows.pali: Gopphakaṭṭhīni baddhakīḷāgoḷakasaṇṭhānāni.
rows.english: 103. The ankle bones are the shape of [two] play balls bound together.

rows.pali: Jaṅghaṭṭhīnaṃ gopphakaṭṭhīsu patiṭṭhitaṭṭhānaṃ apanītatacasindikaḷīrasaṇṭhānaṃ.
rows.english: The shin bones, in the place where they rest on the ankle bones, are the shape of a sindi shoot without the skin removed.

rows.pali: Khuddakajaṅghaṭṭhikaṃ dhanukadaṇḍasaṇṭhānaṃ.
rows.english: The small shin bone is the shape of a[toy] bow stick.

rows.pali: Mahantaṃ milātasappapiṭṭhisaṇṭhānaṃ.
rows.english: The large one is the shape of a shrivelled snake’s back.

rows.pali: Jaṇṇukaṭṭhi ekato parikkhīṇapheṇakasaṇṭhānaṃ.
rows.english: The knee bone is the shape of a lump of froth melted on one side.

rows.pali: Tattha jaṅghaṭṭhikassa patiṭṭhitaṭṭhānaṃ atikhiṇaggagosiṅgasaṇṭhānaṃ.
rows.english: Herein, the place where the shin bone rests on it is the shape of a blunt cow’s horn.

rows.pali: Ūruṭṭhi duttacchitavāsiparasudaṇḍasaṇṭhānaṃ.
rows.english: The thigh bone is the shape of a badly-pared25 handle for an axe or hatchet.

rows.pali: Tassa kaṭiṭṭhimhi patiṭṭhitaṭṭhānaṃ kīḷāgoḷakasaṇṭhānaṃ.
rows.english: The place where it fits into the hip bone is the shape of a play ball.

rows.pali: Tena kaṭiṭṭhino patiṭṭhitaṭṭhānaṃ aggacchinnamahāpunnāgaphalasaṇṭhānaṃ.
rows.english: The place in the hip bone where it is set is the shape of a big punnāga fruit with the end cut off.

rows.pali: Kaṭiṭṭhīni dvepi ekābaddhāni hutvā kumbhakārikauddhanasaṇṭhānāni.
rows.english: 104. The two hip bones, when fastened together,

rows.pali: Pāṭiyekkaṃ kammārakūṭayottakasaṇṭhānāni.
rows.english: are the shape of the ring- fastening of a smith’s hammer.

rows.pali: Koṭiyaṃ ṭhitaṃ ānisadaṭṭhi adhomukhaṃ katvā gahitasappaphaṇasaṇṭhānaṃ, sattaṭṭhaṭṭhānesu chiddāvachiddaṃ.
rows.english: The buttock bone on the end [of them] is the shape of an inverted snake’s hood. It is perforated in seven or eight places.

rows.pali: Piṭṭhikaṇṭakaṭṭhīni abbhantarato uparūpari ṭhapitasīsapaṭṭaveṭhakasaṇṭhānāni.
rows.english: The spine bones are internally the shape of lead-sheet pipes put one on top of the other;

rows.pali: Bāhirato vaṭṭanāvaḷisaṇṭhānāni.
rows.english: externally they are the shape of a string of beads.

rows.pali: Tesaṃ antarantarā kakacadantasadisā dve tayo kaṇṭakā honti.
rows.english: They have two or three rows of projections next to each other like the teeth of a saw.

rows.pali: Catuvīsatiyā phāsukaṭṭhīsu aparipuṇṇāni aparipuṇṇaasisaṇṭhānāni.
rows.english: 105.Of the twenty-four rib bones, the incomplete ones are the shape of incomplete sabres,

rows.pali: Paripuṇṇāni paripuṇṇaasisaṇṭhānāni.
rows.english: and the complete ones are the shape of complete sabres;

rows.pali: Sabbānipi odātakukkuṭassa pasāritapakkhasaṇṭhānāni.
rows.english: all together they are like the outspread wings of a white cock.

rows.pali: Cuddasa uraṭṭhīni jiṇṇasandamānikapañjarasaṇṭhānāni.
rows.english: The fourteen breast bones are the shape of an old chariot frame.26

rows.pali: Hadayaṭṭhi dabbiphaṇasaṇṭhānaṃ.
rows.english: The heart bone (sternum) is the shape of the bowl of a spoon.

rows.pali: Akkhakaṭṭhīni khuddakalohavāsidaṇḍasaṇṭhānāni.
rows.english: The collar bones are the shape of small metal knife handles.

rows.pali: Koṭṭaṭṭhīni ekato parikkhīṇasīhaḷakuddālasaṇṭhānāni.
rows.english: The shoulder- blade bones are the shape of a Sinhalese hoe worn down on one side.

rows.pali: Bāhuṭṭhīni ādāsadaṇḍakasaṇṭhānāni.
rows.english: 106. The upper-arm bones are the shape of looking glass handles.

rows.pali: Aggabāhuṭṭhīni yamakatālakandasaṇṭhānāni.
rows.english: The forearm bones are the shape of a twin palm’s trunks.

rows.pali: Maṇibandhaṭṭhīni ekato alliyāpetvā ṭhapitasīsakapaṭṭaveṭhakasaṇṭhānāni.
rows.english: The wrist bones are the shape of lead-sheet pipes stuck together.

rows.pali: Piṭṭhihatthaṭṭhīni koṭṭitakandalakandarāsisaṇṭhānāni.
rows.english: The bones of the back of the hand are the shape of a bundle of bruised yams.

rows.pali: Hatthaṅgulīsu mūlapabbaṭṭhīni paṇavasaṇṭhānāni.
rows.english: As to the fingers, the bones of the base sections are the shape of small drums;

rows.pali: Majjhapabbaṭṭhīni aparipuṇṇapanasaṭṭhisaṇṭhānāni.
rows.english: those of the middle sections are the shape of immature jackfruit seeds;

rows.pali: Aggapabbaṭṭhīni katakabījasaṇṭhānāni.
rows.english: those of the end sections are the shape of kataka seeds.

rows.pali: Satta gīvaṭṭhīni daṇḍena vijjhitvā paṭipāṭiyā ṭhapitavaṃsakaḷīracakkalakasaṇṭhānāni.
rows.english: 107. The seven neck bones are the shape of rings of bamboo stem threaded one after the other on a stick.

rows.pali: Heṭṭhimahanukaṭṭhi kammārānaṃ ayokūṭayottakasaṇṭhānaṃ.
rows.english: The lower jawbone is the shape of a smith’s iron hammer ring-fastening.

rows.pali: Uparimaṃ avalekhanasatthakasaṇṭhānaṃ.
rows.english: The upper one is the shape of a knife for scraping [the rind off sugarcanes].

rows.pali: Akkhikūpanāsakūpaṭṭhīni apanītamiñjataruṇatālaṭṭhisaṇṭhānāni.
rows.english: The bones of the eye sockets and nostril sockets are the shape of young palmyra seeds with the kernels removed.
